name: Ragdoll System
description: A body as several bodies that disagree with each other politely. Limbs are rigid parts joined by constrained joints, and the interesting decisions are all about what happens when the solver cannot satisfy every constraint at once: iteration count trades stability for cost, and a limit on separation is what stops a ragdoll exploding when two constraints fight. Blending between animated and simulated is the feature that makes ragdolls usable rather than a death effect — a body can go limp progressively — which is why the blend is an input rather than a boolean. movement.character_body still owns the single upright body; this owns the collection that stops being upright.

inputs.name: limbs
inputs.description: Body parts with their masses, shapes and parent joints. Required — a skeleton is content.

inputs.name: solverIterations
inputs.description: Constraint passes per step. More is stabler and slower; below about six a ragdoll starts to jitter.

inputs.name: maxJointSeparation
inputs.description: Distance a joint may be pulled apart before it is hard-clamped, which is what stops a body exploding when constraints fight.

inputs.name: animationBlend
inputs.description: 0 fully simulated, 1 fully animated. Values between are how a body goes limp progressively rather than instantly.

outputs.name: settled
outputs.description: Whether the body has come to rest.

outputs.name: strainByJoint
outputs.description: Constraint error per joint, for debugging and for breaking.
